[LLM] Path-traversal exploit hitting Vitest /__vitest_attachment__ endpoint (CVE-2026-47429 PoC) Exploitation High
Hunts HTTP requests to the Vitest UI server's /__vitest__/ or /__vitest_attachment__ endpoints carrying the Windows-specific '\?\..\' path-traversal payload (or URL-encoded equivalents). This is the literal PoC URL from the advisory bypassing isFileServingAllowed. Rationale: PoC §3 in the advisory uses the literal URL '/__vitest_attachment__?path=...?\..\..\secret.txt'. The '?\..\' sequence is article-specific because the bypass relies on Windows-only quirk (Linux errors on '?' directory). URL-encoded variants %3F%5C..%5C are what curl/browsers send on wire. Cross-checked the vendor advisory and the related Vite CVE-2026-39363 confirming the dev-server-traversal family pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp • https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/security/advisories/GHSA-9crc-q9x8-hgqq • https://securityonline.info/vite-vulnerabilities-cve-2026-39364-arbitrary-file-read/
ATT&CKT1190 T1083 T1006
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemotePort == 51204 or LocalPort == 51204 or RemoteUrl has "__vitest"
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("__vitest_attachment__","__vitest__")
| where RemoteUrl matches regex @"(?i)(%3F%5C|%3F/|\?\\|\?/)\.\.[\\/]"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, LocalIP, LocalPort, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
// Primary: W3C IIS / reverse-proxy logs in front of the Vitest UI host
let TraversalRx = @"(?i)(%3F%5C|%3F/|\?\\|\?/)\.\.[\\/]";
(union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where csUriStem has_any ("__vitest_attachment__","__vitest__")
    | where strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery) matches regex TraversalRx
    | extend Url = strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery), SrcIp = cIP, DstHost = Computer, Method = csMethod, Status = scStatus, UserAgent = csUserAgent
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp, DstHost, sPort, Method, Url, Status, UserAgent, Source="W3CIISLog"),
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where RequestURL has_any ("__vitest_attachment__","__vitest__")
    | where RequestURL matches regex TraversalRx
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp=SourceIP, DstHost=DestinationHostName, sPort=DestinationPort, Method=RequestMethod, Url=RequestURL, Status=tostring(EventOutcome), UserAgent=RequestClientApplication, Source="CommonSecurityLog"),
  (ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where Url has_any ("__vitest_attachment__","__vitest__")
    | where Url matches regex TraversalRx
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, DstHost=DstHostname, sPort=DstPortNumber, Method=HttpMethod, Url, Status=tostring(HttpStatusCode), UserAgent=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, Source="ImWebSession"))
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Post-exploit shell spawned by Vitest node.exe via rerun / saveTestFile (CVE-2026-47429) Exploitation Medium
Hunts node.exe processes whose command line contains 'vitest' spawning interactive shells, script hosts, or LOLBins. This is the post-exploitation shape when an attacker uses the rerun API to execute attacker-controlled test files written via saveTestFile — equivalent to arbitrary code execution. Rationale: Article §Details: 'it's possible to run arbitrary script by writing a script as a test file using saveTestFile and running it using rerun. This means exposing the API / Vitest UI is equivalent to giving script execution access.' The execution surface is node.exe (the vitest runner) spawning whatever the attacker's malicious test file invokes. Pivoting on parent=node.exe + parent cmdline contains 'vitest' + non-test child binary is the cleanest article-grounded shape. Cross-checked vendor advisory. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp • https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/security/advisories/GHSA-9crc-q9x8-hgqq
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.003 T1190

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "vitest"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","net.exe","whoami.exe","hostname.exe","systeminfo.exe","nslookup.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
// Reduce FP: vitest legitimately launches node.exe worker children — only flag non-node children
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith @"\node.exe"
| where NewProcessName has_any (@"\cmd.exe",@"\powershell.exe",@"\pwsh.exe",@"\wscript.exe",@"\cscript.exe",@"\mshta.exe",@"\rundll32.exe",@"\regsvr32.exe",@"\bitsadmin.exe",@"\certutil.exe",@"\curl.exe",@"\wget.exe",@"\whoami.exe",@"\hostname.exe",@"\systeminfo.exe",@"\nslookup.exe")
| where Account !endswith "$"
// Join to a recent vitest invocation on the same host
| join kind=inner (
    SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where CommandLine has "vitest"
    | project VitestTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, VitestPid=NewProcessId, VitestCmd=CommandLine
  ) on Computer
| where TimeGenerated between (VitestTime .. VitestTime + 8h)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, VitestCmd

[LLM] Inbound TCP connection to Vitest UI port 51204 from non-loopback source Delivery Medium
Hunts inbound TCP connections to TCP/51204 (Vitest UI default) on endpoints from non-loopback peers — the observable signal that a misconfigured Vitest UI is being reached over the network. Pair with UC1 (the cmdline misconfiguration) for confirmation. Rationale: Article §PoC step 1 uses default 'http://localhost:51204/' — 51204 is Vitest UI's hard-coded default port. Any inbound to that port from non-loopback on a node.exe-driven listener is by definition the exposure path the advisory warns about. Cross-checked the vitest docs and the related GHSA-9crc-q9x8-hgqq advisory which references the same default port. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp • https://vitest.dev/config/api.html • https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/security/advisories/GHSA-9crc-q9x8-hgqq
ATT&CKT1133 T1190
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where LocalPort == 51204 and Protocol == "Tcp"
| where ActionType in ("InboundConnectionAccepted","ConnectionSuccess","ListeningConnectionCreated")
| where RemoteIPType != "Loopback" and RemoteIP !in ("127.0.0.1","::1","")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), ConnCount=count(), RemoteIps=make_set(RemoteIP, 20)
          by DeviceName, LocalIP, LocalPort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by FirstSeen desc
// Sentinel sees this via ASIM ImNetworkSession (or vendor-specific firewall in CommonSecurityLog)
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstPortNumber == 51204 and NetworkProtocol =~ "tcp"
| where DvcAction in~ ("Allow","Allowed","Accept","") or isempty(DvcAction)
| where SrcIpAddr !in ("127.0.0.1","::1")
| where not(ipv4_is_in_range(SrcIpAddr, "127.0.0.0/8"))
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Sessions=count(), DstHosts=make_set(DstHostname, 20)
          by SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DstPortNumber
| order by FirstSeen desc

description: Inbound TCP connection accepted on port 51204 (Vitest UI default) from a non-loopback source — the network-side observable of CVE-2026-47429 exposure.

level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationPort:51204 -@SourceIp:(127.0.0.1 OR ::1) -CIDR(@SourceIp, 127.0.0.0/8) @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\NODE.EXE)

| NOT (RemoteAddressIP4=/^(127\.|::1)/)

| filter not (srcAddr like /^127\./ or srcAddr = "::1")

Red Hat npm Packages Compromised to Spread a Credential-Stealing Worm

2026-06-01 11 use cases 5 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Multiple official @redhat-cloud-services npm packages were compromised with a credential-stealing worm derived from the open-sourced Mini Shai-Hulud malware, targeting cloud credentials, and developer tooling across CI/CD pipelines. Category: Vulnerabilities & Threats

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Install or update of @redhat-cloud-services npm package post-2026-06-01 (IOC version watchlist)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Red Hat npm Packages Compromised to Spread a Credential-Stealing Worm
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Miasma worm index.js SHA256 IOC hit (Mini Shai-Hulud variant) · [LLM] npm preinstall hook spawns node index.js under @redhat-cloud-services package path · Suspicious browser extension installation · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] node child of npm install initiating outbound network to non-registry destination
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] node child of npm/yarn/pnpm reading cloud and CI credential files (Miasma sweep) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process
[LLM] Miasma worm index.js SHA256 IOC hit (Mini Shai-Hulud variant) Installation High
Hash-based alert on the two published SHA256s for the Miasma payload dropped inside compromised @redhat-cloud-services npm packages. Any host that has touched either file has executed the preinstall and must be treated as having leaked every secret reachable from that build context. Rationale: Anchored on the two SHA256s pre-extracted from the article (Miasma index.js payload). Hash match is unambiguous — these strings only exist in the worm-laced package.

[LLM] npm preinstall hook spawns node index.js under @redhat-cloud-services package path Installation High
Catches the Miasma execution pattern: npm/yarn/pnpm/npx invokes node with index.js inside a node_modules\@redhat-cloud-services\<pkg>\ path during dependency install, which is exactly the preinstall lifecycle hook the compromised manifests declare. Equivalent shape works for any future Mini Shai-Hulud variant. Rationale: Anchors on the article's verbatim preinstall script (`"preinstall": "node index.js"`) and the @redhat-cloud-services scope (Code Blocks 1-3). Process tree (npm/yarn/pnpm/npx → node + cmd-line `index.js` inside the affected scope path) avoids the FPs you'd get from a bare `node index.js` rule.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","npm","yarn","yarn.cmd","pnpm","pnpm.cmd","npx","npx.cmd","corepack.exe","corepack")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "index.js"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "@redhat-cloud-services" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "@redhat-cloud-services" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "@redhat-cloud-services" or FolderPath has "@redhat-cloud-services"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ChildImage = FolderPath, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "node.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith @"\node" or ActingProcessName =~ "node"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","npm","yarn.cmd","yarn","pnpm.cmd","pnpm","npx.cmd","npx","corepack")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "index.js"

| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256

[LLM] node child of npm/yarn/pnpm reading cloud and CI credential files (Miasma sweep) Actions on Objectives High
Hunts the Miasma credential-stealing stage: a `node.exe` instance whose parent is npm/yarn/pnpm/npx touches three or more of the secret stores listed in the Aikido article (.aws, .ssh, .npmrc, .docker, kubeconfig/.kube, gcloud, .env, .azure). A clean preinstall script never sweeps developer secret files. Rationale: Aikido article explicitly enumerates: GITHUB_TOKEN, ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN, AWS keys, GCP ADC + service-account JSON, Azure SP creds, Vault tokens, kubeconfig, npm/PyPI tokens, SSH private keys, Docker registry creds, GPG keys, and .env files. The detection translates that list 1:1 into the file paths each lives at, plus the parent-chain constraint (node under npm/yarn/pnpm/npx) that turns this into a high-fidelity supply-chain signal rather than a routine `cat ~/.aws/credentials` from a dev shell.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1552.005 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let CredPaths = dynamic([@"\.aws\credentials", @"\.aws\config", @"\.ssh\id_", @"\.npmrc", @"\.docker\config.json", @"\.kube\config", "kubeconfig", @"\.config\gcloud", @"\.azure\", @"\.gnupg\", @"\.env", "/.aws/credentials", "/.aws/config", "/.ssh/id_", "/.npmrc", "/.docker/config.json", "/.kube/config", "/.config/gcloud", "/.azure/", "/.gnupg/", "/.env"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","npm","yarn","yarn.cmd","pnpm","pnpm.cmd","npx","npx.cmd","corepack.exe","corepack","bash","sh","zsh","runner.worker","Runner.Worker")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileOpened","FileAccessed")
| extend MatchedPath = tostring(array_iff(CredPaths, FolderPath has_any (CredPaths) or strcat(FolderPath, FileName) has_any (CredPaths)))
| where FolderPath has_any (CredPaths) or strcat(FolderPath, "\\", FileName) has_any (CredPaths)
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), DistinctPaths = dcount(strcat(FolderPath, FileName)), SamplePaths = make_set(strcat(FolderPath, FileName), 20), ParentCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessId, bin(Timestamp, 10m)
| where DistinctPaths >= 3
| order by FirstSeen desc
let CredPaths = dynamic([@"\.aws\credentials", @"\.aws\config", @"\.ssh\id_", @"\.npmrc", @"\.docker\config.json", @"\.kube\config", "kubeconfig", @"\.config\gcloud", @"\.azure\", @"\.gnupg\", @"\.env", "/.aws/credentials", "/.aws/config", "/.ssh/id_", "/.npmrc", "/.docker/config.json", "/.kube/config", "/.config/gcloud", "/.azure/", "/.gnupg/", "/.env"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "node.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "/node" or ActingProcessName =~ "node"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm","yarn","pnpm","npx","preinstall","postinstall","index.js")

| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), DistinctPaths = dcount(TargetFilePath), SamplePaths = make_set(TargetFilePath, 20), Cmd = any(ActingProcessCommandLine) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessId, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where DistinctPaths >= 3
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:(linux.auditd OR windows.sysmon) (@process.name:node OR @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE OR */node)) (@auditd.path:*/.aws/credentials* OR @auditd.path:*/.aws/config* OR @auditd.path:*/.ssh/id_* OR @auditd.path:*/.npmrc* OR @auditd.path:*/.docker/config.json* OR @auditd.path:*/.kube/config* OR @auditd.path:*/kubeconfig* OR @auditd.path:*/.config/gcloud* OR @auditd.path:*/.azure/* OR @auditd.path:*/.gnupg/* OR @auditd.path:*/.env* OR @TargetFilename:*\\.aws\\credentials* OR @TargetFilename:*\\.ssh\\id_* OR @TargetFilename:*\\.npmrc* OR @TargetFilename:*\\.kube\\config* OR @TargetFilename:*kubeconfig* OR @TargetFilename:*\\.config\\gcloud* OR @TargetFilename:*\\.docker\\config.json* OR @TargetFilename:*\\.env*)

[LLM] node child of npm install initiating outbound network to non-registry destination Command & Control Medium
Surfaces the Miasma exfiltration step: a node.exe spawned by npm/yarn/pnpm/npx during install opens an outbound socket to anything other than the npm registry, yarn registry, github.com or githubusercontent.com. Honest preinstall scripts almost never call out to arbitrary internet hosts. Rationale: Article describes a 4.2 MB obfuscated payload that exfiltrates harvested secrets — exfiltration must traverse the network, and a clean npm preinstall should only ever talk to the registry/GitHub. Joining the network event back to a node-under-npm process tree via host + PID + 10-minute window is the cleanest way to attribute. Sentinel side joins ImNetworkSession to ImProcessCreate on host + time (ImNetworkSession has no process-name column, so attribution lives in the join, not in a direct field).
ATT&CKT1041 T1071.001 T1567
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let NpmNodeProcs = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","npm","yarn","yarn.cmd","pnpm","pnpm.cmd","npx","npx.cmd","corepack.exe","corepack")
    | project NodeStart = Timestamp, DeviceId, NodePid = ProcessId, NodeCmd = ProcessCommandLine, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where not(RemoteUrl endswith "registry.npmjs.org"
        or RemoteUrl endswith "registry.yarnpkg.com"
        or RemoteUrl endswith "registry.npmmirror.com"
        or RemoteUrl endswith "github.com"
        or RemoteUrl endswith "githubusercontent.com"
        or RemoteUrl endswith "githubapp.com"
        or RemoteUrl endswith "objects.githubusercontent.com"
        or RemoteUrl endswith "nodejs.org"
        or RemoteUrl endswith "pypi.org"
        or RemoteUrl endswith "repo.maven.apache.org")
| join kind=inner NpmNodeProcs on $left.DeviceId == $right.DeviceId, $left.InitiatingProcessId == $right.NodePid
| where Timestamp between (NodeStart .. NodeStart + 10m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, NodeCmd, ParentCmd, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let NodeProcs = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActingProcessName endswith "node.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "/node" or ActingProcessName =~ "node"
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","npm","yarn.cmd","yarn","pnpm.cmd","pnpm","npx.cmd","npx","corepack")
    | project NodeHost = DvcHostname, NodeStart = EventStartTime, NodeCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentCmd = ParentProcessCommandLine;
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where NetworkDirection == "Outbound"
| where isnotempty(DstHostname)
| where not(DstHostname endswith "registry.npmjs.org"
        or DstHostname endswith "registry.yarnpkg.com"
        or DstHostname endswith "registry.npmmirror.com"
        or DstHostname endswith "github.com"
        or DstHostname endswith "githubusercontent.com"
        or DstHostname endswith "githubapp.com"
        or DstHostname endswith "nodejs.org"
        or DstHostname endswith "pypi.org"
        or DstHostname endswith "repo.maven.apache.org")
| join kind=inner NodeProcs on $left.SrcHostname == $right.NodeHost
| where TimeGenerated between (NodeStart .. NodeStart + 10m)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, NodeCmd, ParentCmd, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkBytes
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 (@Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE) OR @process.name:node) -@DestinationHostname:*.npmjs.org -@DestinationHostname:*.yarnpkg.com -@DestinationHostname:*.npmmirror.com -@DestinationHostname:*.github.com -@DestinationHostname:*.githubusercontent.com -@DestinationHostname:*.githubapp.com -@DestinationHostname:*.nodejs.org -@DestinationHostname:*.pypi.org -@DestinationHostname:*.maven.apache.org -CIDR(@DestinationIp, 10.0.0.0/8) -CIDR(@DestinationIp, 172.16.0.0/12) -CIDR(@DestinationIp, 192.168.0.0/16)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest ContextImageFileName=/\\node(\.exe)?$/i NOT (DomainName=/(\.|^)(registry\.npmjs\.org|registry\.yarnpkg\.com|registry\.npmmirror\.com|github\.com|githubusercontent\.com|githubapp\.com|nodejs\.org|pypi\.org|maven\.apache\.org)$/i)
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\node(\.exe)?$/i ParentBaseFileName=/^(npm(\.cmd|\.exe)?|yarn(\.cmd)?|pnpm(\.cmd)?|npx(\.cmd)?|corepack(\.exe)?)$/i | rename(field=TargetProcessId, as=NodePid)}, field=[aid, ContextProcessId], key=[aid, NodePid])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.app IN ("node.exe","node") OR All_Traffic.process_name IN ("node.exe","node")) AND All_Traffic.dest_port IN (80,443,8080,8443) AND All_Traffic.transport="tcp" by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_port _time
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| where NOT match(dest, "(?i)(^|\.)(registry\.npmjs\.org|registry\.yarnpkg\.com|registry\.npmmirror\.com|github\.com|githubusercontent\.com|githubapp\.com|objects\.githubusercontent\.com|nodejs\.org|repo\.maven\.apache\.org|pypi\.org)$")
| join type=inner src [| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("node.exe","node") AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","npm","yarn","yarn.cmd","pnpm","pnpm.cmd","npx","npx.cmd","corepack.exe","corepack") by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process Processes.process _time | rename Processes.dest as src, Processes.parent_process as parent_cmd, Processes.process as node_cmd, _time as node_start | eval node_end = node_start + 600]
| where _time >= node_start AND _time <= node_end
| table _time src user node_cmd parent_cmd dest dest_port
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.app IN ("node.exe","node") OR All_Traffic.process_name IN ("node.exe","node")) AND All_Traffic.dest_port IN (80,443,8080,8443) AND All_Traffic.transport="tcp" by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_port _time
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| where NOT match(dest, "(?i)(^|\.)(registry\.npmjs\.org|registry\.yarnpkg\.com|registry\.npmmirror\.com|github\.com|githubusercontent\.com|githubapp\.com|objects\.githubusercontent\.com|nodejs\.org|repo\.maven\.apache\.org|pypi\.org)$")
| join type=inner src [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("node.exe","node") AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","npm","yarn","yarn.cmd","pnpm","pnpm.cmd","npx","npx.cmd","corepack.exe","corepack") by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process Processes.process _time | rename Processes.dest as src, Processes.parent_process as parent_cmd, Processes.process as node_cmd, _time as node_start | eval node_end = node_start + 600]
| where _time >= node_start AND _time <= node_end
| table _time src user node_cmd parent_cmd dest dest_port
[LLM] Install or update of @redhat-cloud-services npm package post-2026-06-01 (IOC version watchlist) Delivery Medium
File-event hunt for write activity under any node_modules\@redhat-cloud-services\<pkg>\ path on or after 2026-06-01. The runbook then reconciles the package version against the 30 IOC versions enumerated in the Aikido article — that step is too brittle for a single query but the file-write is a clean pivot point. Rationale: All 30 affected package names come straight from the IOC list in the article and the @redhat-cloud-services scope appears verbatim in Code Blocks 1 and 2. Date filter (>= 2026-06-01) matches the published compromise date. Version still needs runbook reconciliation because Defender/Sysmon/auditd file-event records don't expose package.json contents — the rationale is to give analysts a pivot, not a verdict.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let IOCPackages = dynamic(["chrome","compliance-client","config-manager-client","entitlements-client","eslint-config-redhat-cloud-services","frontend-components","frontend-components-advisor-components","frontend-components-config","frontend-components-config-utilities","frontend-components-notifications","frontend-components-remediations","frontend-components-testing","frontend-components-translations","frontend-components-utilities","hcc-feo-mcp","hcc-kessel-mcp","hcc-pf-mcp","host-inventory-client","insights-client","integrations-client","javascript-clients-shared","notifications-client","patch-client","quickstarts-client","rbac-client","remediations-client","rule-components","sources-client","tsc-transform-imports","types","vulnerabilities-client"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp >= datetime(2026-06-01T00:00:00Z)
| where FolderPath has "node_modules" and FolderPath has "@redhat-cloud-services"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| extend Pkg = extract(@"(?i)@redhat-cloud-services[\\/]([^\\/]+)", 1, FolderPath)
| where Pkg in~ (IOCPackages) or isempty(Pkg) == false
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), FileCount = count(), SampleFiles = make_set(strcat(FolderPath, "\\", FileName), 10) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, Pkg
| order by FirstSeen desc
let IOCPackages = dynamic(["chrome","compliance-client","config-manager-client","entitlements-client","eslint-config-redhat-cloud-services","frontend-components","frontend-components-advisor-components","frontend-components-config","frontend-components-config-utilities","frontend-components-notifications","frontend-components-remediations","frontend-components-testing","frontend-components-translations","frontend-components-utilities","hcc-feo-mcp","hcc-kessel-mcp","hcc-pf-mcp","host-inventory-client","insights-client","integrations-client","javascript-clients-shared","notifications-client","patch-client","quickstarts-client","rbac-client","remediations-client","rule-components","sources-client","tsc-transform-imports","types","vulnerabilities-client"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated >= datetime(2026-06-01T00:00:00Z)
| where TargetFilePath has "node_modules" and TargetFilePath has "@redhat-cloud-services"
| where EventType in~ ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileCreate","FileWrite")
| extend Pkg = extract(@"(?i)@redhat-cloud-services[\\/]([^\\/]+)", 1, TargetFilePath)
| where Pkg in~ (IOCPackages)
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), FileCount = count(), SampleFiles = make_set(TargetFilePath, 10) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, Pkg
| order by FirstSeen desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or SHA1 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or MD5 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or SHA1 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or MD5 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

logsource:

      - '\node.exe'
      - '\npm.cmd'
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\npx.cmd'

  selection_scope:
    CommandLine|contains:

level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) (@EventID:1 OR @EventID:4688) (@Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE OR *\\npm.cmd OR *\\NPM.CMD OR *\\npm.exe OR *\\npx.cmd OR *\\npx.exe) OR @ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR *\\npm.cmd OR *\\npm.exe)) @CommandLine:(*@cloudplatform-single-spa* OR *@wb-track* OR *@data-science/* OR *@ce-rwb* OR *@payments-widget* OR *@travel-autotests* OR *@t-in-one* OR *@capibar.chat* OR *@sber-ecom-core*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\(node|npm|npx)(\.exe|\.cmd)?$/i OR ParentBaseFileName=/^(node|npm|npx)(\.exe|\.cmd)?$/i
| regex("@(cloudplatform-single-spa|wb-track|data-science/|ce-rwb|payments-widget|travel-autotests|t-in-one|capibar\.chat|sber-ecom-core)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

[LLM] C2 callback to moika.tech payload distribution infrastructure Command & Control High
Detects outbound HTTPS from any process to oob.moika.tech or the parent moika.tech domain — the dropper fetches its platform-specific payload from https://oob.moika.tech/payload/{win|mac|linux}. Catches the post-install reconnaissance stager regardless of which scope triggered it. Rationale: oob.moika.tech (and the parent moika.tech) is the single C2 endpoint named in the article — every package in the cluster fetches https://oob.moika.tech/payload/<platform>. Domain has no legitimate dev-tooling use and was first seen in this campaign on 2026-05-28.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("oob.moika.tech","moika.tech")
   or RemoteUrl matches regex @"(?i)moika\.tech/payload/(win|mac|linux)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where DestinationHostName has_any ("oob.moika.tech","moika.tech")
         or RequestURL has_any ("oob.moika.tech","moika.tech/payload/")
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceHostName, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor),
  (DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where Name has "moika.tech"
    | project TimeGenerated, ClientIP, Computer, Name, QueryType, Result, ServerIPAddress),
  (ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where HttpHostName has_any ("oob.moika.tech","moika.tech") or Url has "moika.tech/payload/"
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, HttpHostName, Url, HttpMethod, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Malicious postinstall.js dropped under node_modules for actor scopes Installation High
Detects the obfuscated ~7 KB postinstall.js stager being materialised inside node_modules/@<actor-scope>/<pkg>/scripts/postinstall.js. Hunting tier because file-event volume from npm installs is high — the value is in retrospective hunts and forensic timeline reconstruction. Rationale: The article specifies `scripts/postinstall.js` as the obfuscated stager, dropped under each malicious scoped package. Pairing the literal filename with the actor's nine scope strings inside node_modules yields a near-zero-FP file event because no legitimate package would publish under these namespaces.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1546.016
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FileName =~ "postinstall.js"
| where FolderPath has "node_modules"
| where FolderPath has_any (
    "@cloudplatform-single-spa","@wb-track","@data-science",
    "@ce-rwb","@payments-widget","@travel-autotests",
    "@t-in-one","@capibar.chat","@sber-ecom-core")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, FileSize,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFileName =~ "postinstall.js"
| where TargetFilePath has "node_modules"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (
    "@cloudplatform-single-spa","@wb-track","@data-science",
    "@ce-rwb","@payments-widget","@travel-autotests",
    "@t-in-one","@capibar.chat","@sber-ecom-core")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSize, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] node.exe spawns detached child from tmpdir after npm install (moika.tech dropper) Installation Medium
After fetching the platform payload, the obfuscated stager writes it to the OS tmpdir and spawns a detached child. Detects node.exe spawning a process whose image lives in %TEMP% / %TMP% / /tmp where the grandparent chain involves npm — catches stage-2 even if the C2 domain rotates. Rationale: Article describes the deobfuscated execution flow: stager fetches payload from oob.moika.tech, writes it to tmpdir, then spawns a detached child. Constraining node.exe parent + tmpdir child path + correlation with a recent npm install on the same host turns a noisy primitive (node spawning anything) into a campaign-specific signal.
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1105 T1564.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let NpmHosts = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where FileName in~ ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd")
        or ProcessCommandLine has "npm install"
    | project DeviceId, NpmTime = Timestamp;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where FolderPath has_any (
    @"\AppData\Local\Temp\",
    @"\Windows\Temp\",
    "/tmp/",
    "/var/folders/")
| where FileName !in~ ("conhost.exe","node.exe")
| join kind=inner NpmHosts on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (NpmTime .. NpmTime + 30m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          NpmTime, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, NpmTime)
| order by Timestamp desc
let NpmHosts = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName endswith "\\npm.cmd" or NewProcessName endswith "\\npm.exe" or CommandLine has "npm install"
    | project Computer, NpmTime = TimeGenerated;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\node.exe"
| where NewProcessName has_any (
    @"\AppData\Local\Temp\",
    @"\Windows\Temp\",
    "/tmp/")
| where NewProcessName !endswith "\\conhost.exe" and NewProcessName !endswith "\\node.exe"
| join kind=inner NpmHosts on Computer
| where TimeGenerated between (NpmTime .. NpmTime + 30m)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, NpmTime, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, NpmTime)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE) @Image:(*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\* OR *\\Windows\\Temp\\* OR */tmp/* OR */var/folders/*) -@Image:(*\\conhost.exe OR *\\node.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^node\.exe$/i
| regex("(\\\\Temp\\\\|\\\\AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp\\\\|/tmp/|/var/folders/)", field=ImageFileName)
| NOT (ImageFileName=/\\(conhost|node)\.exe$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="node.exe" AND (Processes.process_path="*\\Temp\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*" OR Processes.process_path="/tmp/*" OR Processes.process_path="/var/folders/*") by _time Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | join type=inner dest [| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="npm.cmd" OR Processes.process_name="npm.exe" OR Processes.process="*npm install*") earliest=-30m latest=+1m by Processes.dest Processes.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename count as npm_count] | where npm_count > 0
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="node.exe" AND (Processes.process_path="*\\Temp\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*" OR Processes.process_path="/tmp/*" OR Processes.process_path="/var/folders/*") by _time Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | join type=inner dest [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="npm.cmd" OR Processes.process_name="npm.exe" OR Processes.process="*npm install*") earliest=-30m latest=+1m by Processes.dest Processes.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename count as npm_count] | where npm_count > 0
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count

    category: process_creation

            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416: PATCH /workspaces/{id}/members/{user_id} role-change request Exploitation High
Hunts the core privilege-escalation primitive in CVE-2026-47416 — an HTTP PATCH against /workspaces/<workspace_id>/members/<user_id> on praisonai-platform <=0.1.2. Because require_workspace_member defaults to min_role='member' and the route never overrides it, any authenticated member can write {"role":"owner"} to any member row. Outside of one-off legitimate owner-driven role tweaks this URL+verb pair is extremely rare, so even URI-only telemetry is high-fidelity for affected deployments. Rationale: Article pinpoints the exact endpoint shape (PATCH /workspaces/{workspace_id}/members/{user_id}) and the route file (api/routes/workspaces.py:115-127). Even without request-body visibility, the verb+path pair is rare enough on praisonai-platform to be high-fidelity; restricting on HTTP 2xx removes 401/403 noise from unaffected versions. Cross-checked against the GHSA advisory body and corroborated by independent PraisonAI security coverage on cybersecuritynews.com and Sysdig confirming the platform's pattern of weakly-gated workspace endpoints. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c2m8-4gcg-v22g • https://cybersecuritynews.com/praisonai-vulnerability-exploited/ • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/cve-2026-44338-praisonai-authentication-bypass-in-under-4-hours-and-the-growing-trend-of-rapid-exploitation

title: praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416 PATCH workspaces members role-change
id: 7a4cbf8e-2b39-4b9a-a4ba-2026474160c1
status: experimental
description: Detects HTTP PATCH requests against the praisonai-platform /workspaces/{workspace_id}/members/{user_id} endpoint that exposes a vertical privilege-escalation primitive (CVE-2026-47416). The endpoint should normally see near-zero PATCH traffic; any successful PATCH is suspicious until the deployment is patched to >=0.1.3 with the min_role='owner' gate applied.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c2m8-4gcg-v22g
author: SOC Detection Engineering

  - Legitimate workspace owner changing another member's role via the official UI (will be rare and identifiable by the originating account being an existing owner)
  - Internal admin scripts that pre-seed workspace ownership during tenant provisioning

[LLM] praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416: Member self-promotion + legitimate-owner demotion chain within one hour Installation High
Catches the two-request takeover chain described in the advisory — the attacker first self-promotes (PATCH on their own user_id with {"role":"owner"}) and then demotes the legitimate owner (PATCH on the owner's user_id with {"role":"member"}). This temporal pivot is much higher fidelity than UC1 because legitimate workspace operations almost never produce two role-mutating PATCHs from the same client IP within a short window. Rationale: The advisory explicitly calls out the two-PATCH primitive: 'owner lockout in two requests total'. Workspaces where the same client IP/user mutates 2+ distinct member rows within the hour is a behaviour the legitimate UI essentially never produces — owners normally change one role at a time and rarely demote themselves seconds after promoting. Threshold of >=2 distinct TargetUser within 60m is the article's own attack cadence. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c2m8-4gcg-v22g
ATT&CKT1098 T1531 T1136.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let Lookback = 7d;
let WindowMin = 60m;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where HttpMethod =~ "PATCH"
| where Url matches regex @"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/members/[^/?#]+"
| where HttpStatusCode in ("200","204")
| extend Workspace = extract(@"(?i)/workspaces/([^/]+)/members/", 1, Url)
| extend TargetUser = extract(@"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/members/([^/?#]+)", 1, Url)
| summarize PatchCount = count(),
            TargetsTouched = dcount(TargetUser),
            Targets = make_set(TargetUser, 10),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Workspace, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin)
| where PatchCount >= 2 and TargetsTouched >= 2   // self-promote + owner-demote = 2 distinct user_ids
| extend WindowMinutes = datetime_diff('minute', LastSeen, FirstSeen)
| order by FirstSeen desc

[LLM] praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416: Bulk agent/issue/project/comment enumeration immediately after a workspace role-change PATCH Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the collection phase of the takeover chain — once the attacker holds owner via the CVE-2026-47416 primitive they pivot into LIST endpoints (agents, issues, projects, comments) that were previously gated by owner-tier access. The detection joins a successful PATCH on /workspaces/*/members/* with a burst of GET/LIST traffic from the same session within 15 minutes, flagging the post-elevation data harvest. Rationale: Article explicitly chains the elevation into 'exfiltrate everything via the agent/issue/project/comment IDORs that were filed as separate advisories'. The named LIST endpoints come from the advisory's own corroboration section. Pairing the elevation event with the post-elevation enumeration inside 15 minutes weeds out generic browse traffic from a non-attack owner. Burst threshold of 10 distinct GETs is calibrated to the article's described mass-pull behaviour rather than a casual single-resource read. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c2m8-4gcg-v22g
ATT&CKT1213 T1530 T1087.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let Lookback = 7d;
let PostWindow = 15m;
let BurstThreshold = 10;   // 10+ list calls inside 15m post-PATCH = harvest-shaped
let RoleChanges = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where HttpMethod =~ "PATCH"
    | where Url matches regex @"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/members/[^/?#]+"
    | where HttpStatusCode in ("200","204")
    | project PatchTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, PatchedWorkspace = extract(@"(?i)/workspaces/([^/]+)/members/", 1, Url);
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where HttpMethod =~ "GET"
| where Url matches regex @"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/(agents|issues|projects|comments)"
| join kind=inner RoleChanges on SrcIpAddr
| where TimeGenerated between (PatchTime .. PatchTime + PostWindow)
| summarize ListCount = count(),
            DistinctResources = dcount(extract(@"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/(agents|issues|projects|comments)", 1, Url)),
            ListUrls = make_set(Url, 25),
            FirstList = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastList = max(TimeGenerated)
            by SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, PatchedWorkspace, PatchTime
| where ListCount >= BurstThreshold
| extend DelaySeconds = datetime_diff('second', FirstList, PatchTime)
| order by PatchTime desc

// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-47416")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-47416")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
